newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca up amid talk of Sanofi merger.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca up amid talk of Sanofi merger.

text.p: Shares in Zeneca Plc were among the biggest percentage gainers in the UK market in early trading on Friday amid talk of a merger with Sanofi of France.

Elf Aquitaine said yesterday it wanted to sell part of its 53 percent stake in Sanofi and wanted it to merge with another drug group -- sparking talk of an alliance with Zeneca or Warner-Lambert Co of the United States.
Zeneca shares rose as much as 29-1/2p or 1.8 percent in early trading -- outpacing an opening 1.1 percent rise in the FTSE 100 index -- before drifting off to be up 12p at 16.42-1/2 stg by 0847 GMT.
The gain built on a $2-3/4 rise in Zeneca's ADRs in the U.S. yesterday.
Zeneca has been a perennial subject of bid speculation since its demerger from Imperial Chemical Industries Plc two years ago, amid a spate of bids and mergers in the world pharmaceutical industry.
Analysts said a merger with Sanofi was possible and could be a good fit with Zeneca. The French company's cardio-vascular drugs were seen as particularly complementary to Zeneca's activities.
But they cautioned that no bid or merger involving Zeneca had yet emerged, despite two years of speculation.
Said one: "A merger with Sanofi would be do-able and would be good for Zeneca."

Another added: "Zeneca is the stock that everybody predicted would do something on the corporate side because of its relatively small size, and after what Elf said yesterday people are looking at Sanofi as well. People are putting two and two together."
Analysts added that the gain in the ADRs in the U.S. on Thursday had helped push its shares up and said Zeneca shares should continue to be well supported by its growth prospects.
"You could justify the current share price on fundamentals alone," the second analyst said.
